neighbours.label: the word that starts a follow-on clause in conversational text: a question tacked onto a prompt ('Tell us about X, how …', '? Or will …') or 'and then <verb>' continuing an action
fire: Welcome to the show. Tell us about your childhood, how did growing up on a farm shape your writing?
She did not simply read the report once at the start and then forget it; she kept returning to it all year.
Is the course open to beginners? Or will I need some experience before I sign up?
Tell us about the band, how did the four of you end up playing together?
It was good that he did not just write the rules on day one and then ignore them; we discussed them weekly.
Does the ticket include lunch? Or will we have to bring our own food?
Tell us about your first job, how would you describe it to someone who has never worked in a kitchen?
The essay could open with the main claim and then outline the evidence that supports it.
quiet: Welcome to the show. Her childhood on a farm in Iowa shaped much of her early writing.
She read the report once at the start of the year, during a long flight to Singapore.
The course is open to beginners with no previous experience of painting.
The four members of the band met at a music school in Leeds.
He wrote the rules on a large sheet of paper on day one of the camp.
The ticket includes lunch at the cafe beside the museum.
Her first job was washing dishes in the kitchen of a seaside hotel.
The essay opens with a claim about the evidence for early farming in the valley.
